$$\frac{4}{(x-3)} + \frac{2}{(x+7)} = (px+q)/((x-3)(x+7))$$

The equation above is true for all $x > 3$, where $p$ and $q$ are positive constants. What is the value of $pq$?
explanation: Choice A is correct. To add the fractions on the left side, find a common denominator of $(x-3)(x+7)$: $\frac{4(x+7) + 2(x-3)}{(x-3)(x+7)} = \frac{4x + 28 + 2x - 6}{(x-3)(x+7)} = \frac{6x + 22}{(x-3)(x+7)}$. Comparing with $\frac{px + q}{(x-3)(x+7)}$: $p = 6$ and $q = 22$. Therefore, $pq = 6 \times 22 = 132$.
